public_rationale: Ars Technica reported on June 16, 2026 that OpenAI had $13.07 billion in revenue and $20.92 billion in operating losses for 2025 [e1]. These figures imply about $2.60 in operating expenses per revenue dollar, below $3 under that accounting interpretation [e1]. This comparison does not establish a ratio on the claim's unspecified spending basis, comparable ratios across the intended company group, or whether subsidies were necessary for growth [e1]. The evidence therefore leaves the claim unresolved [e1].
limitations: The comparison uses reported operating results, not a defined measure of the claimed spending or product subsidies [e1].
The evidence covers OpenAI's 2025 finances and does not establish spending ratios for the other companies or growth without subsidies [e1].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The growth of the AI companies in question is only possible because all of them heavily subsidize their products, spending $3 to $15 for every dollar of revenue.
conditions: all of the companies in question (the 'fastest-growing' AI companies boosters cite)

statement.excerpt: That “growth” is only possible because all of the companies in question heavily subsidize their products, spending $3 to $15 for every dollar of revenue.

from_speaker: all of the companies in question
spending $3 to $15 for every dollar of revenue
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading concerns rapidly growing generative-AI vendors, including OpenAI and Anthropic, rather than every company supplying AI infrastructure.
The claim combines a spending ratio with a stronger assertion that subsidies are necessary for growth. Losses alone do not establish that necessity.
I use calendar 2025, the latest completed annual reporting period before the post, consistent with the surrounding discussion of annual revenue.
Spending means company-wide expenditure relative to realized revenue. The speaker does not specify cash expenditure, accounting expenses, treatment of investment, or an accounting basis.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable records show spending of $3–$15 per dollar of realized revenue for every company in the intended group, and credible evidence shows that their growth depended on those subsidies.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A company clearly within the intended group has a comparable spending ratio outside the stated range, or credible evidence shows that its growth continued without the claimed subsidy dependence.
